 Stephen Leo Siciliano
 February 14, 1945 – October 18, 2026 
 IN THE CARE OF National Funeral Home & Memorial Park 
 Stephen Leo Siciliano, 81, of Reston, Virginia, passed away October 18 with his family at his side. He is survived by his beloved wife of 54 years, Abbey (Schulman), and his sons Andrew and Seth (wife Elizabeth); grandchildren Lucy, Isla, and Henry; and siblings Leo, Mary Ann (husband Robert), and Catherine.
 Stephen was born in Johnstown, Pennsylvania on February 14, 1945 to Mary and Leo Siciliano. He grew up in Cleveland, Ohio. After graduating from the Cathedral Latin School, he earned an undergraduate degree from John Carroll University and a Juris Doctor from Northwestern University. Stephen then proudly served his country for four years as a captain in the United States Army. He was awarded a Bronze Star during his service in Vietnam.
 After leaving the Army, Stephen married Abbey, started a family, and settled in Northern Virginia. For thirty-one years he served as a general counsel for the Federal Reserve Board of Governors in Washington, D.C.
 After retiring in 2004, Stephen traveled the world with Abbey and loved spending time with his grandchildren. He was a voracious reader, gifted orator and debater, and student of history. His lifelong quest for knowledge was interrupted daily by the wins and losses of his beloved Cleveland Browns and Guardians.
 Funeral services will be held on October 26 at King David Memorial Gardens in Falls Church, VA, with a reception to follow at the Siciliano home. In lieu of flowers, the family kindly requests donations be made to the Tunnel to Towers Foundation ( t2t.org ) and Hadassah Hospitals ( https://www.hadassah.org ).
